articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Spring Cleanup Across Foundry Row
articles.deck: Residents of Foundry Row filled the hall on Sunday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The Foundry Row Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Gwen Wallace, who has lived in Foundry Row for 15 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. Public works estimates the work will take about 15 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Council Votes on Summer Concert Series After Long Debate
articles.deck: Residents of Bellwood filled the hall on Thursday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The plan calls for summer concert series along Maple Terrace, with work expected to start in May. The Bellwood Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Renee Farrow, who has lived in Bellwood for 16 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Letter: the Mill Hill Lions Club Did a Good Job This Winter
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the March meeting. To the editor: I have lived on Rowan Court for 5 years, and I want to say what a difference the Mill Hill Lions Club has made.
Please keep the community oven in the budget. Many of us on Rowan Court use it every week. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Patrice Thibodeaux, Eastgate

articles.title: Letters: Linden Terrace Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. Please keep the seasonal farmers market in the budget. Many of us on Linden Terrace use it every week.
To the editor: I have lived on Linden Terrace for 11 years, and I want to say what a difference the Eastgate Senior Lunch Program has made.

articles.title: Glen Terrace Repaving Set to Begin in September
articles.deck: Organizers expect about 5 people and say footpath repair is the main draw.
body: The effort began in September when a handful of neighbors met at the Kettle Hill Park gate to talk about footpath repair.

Several residents on Glen Terrace said they had been waiting since 1995 for something like this. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Kettle Hill Park gate on Monday at 7 p.m.
The Eastgate Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

articles.title: Eleanor Kaczmarek, 65, Carpenter
articles.deck: Friends remember Eleanor Kaczmarek for the many years of service to Lower Millrace.
body: Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Lower Millrace. Eleanor Kaczmarek died in May at home on Garden Avenue, at the age of 65.

Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Mill Hill Lions Club in his or her name. Born in Lower Millrace in the years after the war, Eleanor Kaczmarek spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
